review_notes: I read the whole file. The only new concept is the structure `UniformSchwartzDecay`. It is not a competing version of Mathlib's `SchwartzMap`. `SchwartzMap` needs decay of all derivatives for a single function. This structure needs decay only up to order 2, uses the `(1+‖v‖)^N` weight, is uniform over a torus parameter `x`, and also bounds the spatial gradient. It is a Prop-valued, deliberately weaker, parametrised hypothesis, so it is not the same concept under matching assumptions. The decay hypotheses in the helper lemmas (`schwartz_pointwise_decay`, `schwartz_fderiv_component_decay`, `schwartz_poly_weighted_decay`) are stated as raw ∀/∃ propositions, not as new definitions. The integrability lemmas (`inverse_poly_integrable`, `integrable_one_add_norm_pow_mul`, `integrable_of_schwartz_bound`) are theorem-level overlaps with Mathlib results. The rubric excludes those, so I did not report them. I found no independent duplicate definition, and I did not check Mathlib for near-duplicate theorems beyond that. The case for consolidation is unclear, so I abstain.
